title: service-lease-and-middleware-contract-playbook-2027
author: Asha Raman
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines the platform-side middleware contract and the concept of a "service lease" used to manage multi-tenant runtime responsibilities across the Redwood platform. It codifies expectations between service owners and platform operators for telemetry, lifecycle (lease) durations, graceful deprecation, and automated enforcement. The goal is to reduce unplanned operational toil, improve fairness in shared runtime resources, and make automated remediation predictable.

Background and motivation
-------------------------
Problem observed: services are frequently onboarded with implicit assumptions about sidecars, health checks, and telemetry. Over time this produces:
- Missing or inconsistent SLIs for operator tooling.
- Services without an explicit lifecycle or owner contact (stale services consuming routing/eviction credits).
- Hard-to-automate enforcement because contracts are ad-hoc.

Design intent:
- Make runtime expectations explicit in a light-weight contract attached to the service (middleware contract).
- Attach a timeboxed "service lease" to each service. Leases can be renewed by owners or expired and flagged for automated safe-decommission.
- Provide operator-runbook steps and automation primitives to reduce manual intervention.

Scope
-----
This document covers:
- Platform-side middleware contract (telemetry, health, sidecar semantics).
- Service lease lifecycle (registration, renewal, expiry, deprecation).
- Automated enforcement and safe-decommission paths.
- Onboarding checklist, SLO/SLI minimums, and runbook play for operators.
Out of scope: per-customer commercial terms, Dedicated/Private contractual SLAs (those are handled by legal/enterprise ops).

Key definitions
---------------
- Middleware contract: a short, machine-readable declaration attached to a service that specifies required telemetry, health endpoints, and sidecar capabilities.
- Service lease: an expiration timestamp and renewal policy assigned to a service on registration.
- Lease steward: the named owner or rotating team contact responsible for lease renewals.
- Safe-decommission: automated, staged removal procedure with rollback and snapshotting.

Policy summary (one-line)
------------------------
All services running on shared Redwood runtime must present a middleware contract and a valid service lease. Failure to comply will trigger graduated remediation (alerts -> soft isolation -> snapshot + pause).

Middleware contract: minimal schema and expectations
--------------------------------------------------
The middleware contract is a small YAML blob stored as part of service registration. Minimum required fields: owner, contact, sli_set, health_path, lease_expires, sidecar_version. Optional: eviction_priority, prefetch_hint, cost_center.
Example minimal contract (YAML):

  service_name: catalog-api
  owner: team-search
  contact: search-oncall@redwood.ai
  sli_set: [availability, p50-gen-latency, token-cost-per-req]
  health_path: /_status
  lease_expires: 2027-06-30
  sidecar_version: v2.1.0

Minimum telemetry & SLI expectations
-----------------------------------
Services must produce the following telemetry at onboarding and maintain it for the duration of the lease:
1) Availability: uptime (synthetic and real) reported hourly.
2) Latency histograms: p50/p95/p99 for generating endpoints (or equivalent business-critical paths).
3) Token consumption counters (for LLM paths) or request CPU/ms for non-LLM services.
4) Error classification: 4xx, 5xx, model-misfire, downstream-sig-fault.

Minimum SLOs for shared runtime defaults (can be overridden with business justification):
| SLI | Default SLO | Alert threshold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Availability (7d rolling) | 99.9% | < 99.5% -> page |
| p95 latency (in-region) | 200ms (text-only endpoints) | > 350ms -> warn |
| Token cost per 1k | N/A (cost signal) | > baseline * 3 -> investigate |

Service lease lifecycle (operator summary)
-----------------------------------------
1) Registration: service owner provides middleware contract YAML to platform registry. Platform assigns initial lease_expires (default 6 months).
2) Renewal: owner receives email/oncall notice 30d, 14d, 3d before expiry; renewal is single-click or cli command 'platform lease renew <service> --duration 6m'.
3) Lapsed/Expired: on expiry, platform performs non-destructive actions: soft-isolation (traffic limited to 10%), snapshot metrics & prefix caches, create "stale-service" ticket.
4) Post-grace window (14d after expiry): escalate to operator for manual decommission if owner does not respond.
5) Forced safe-decommission: remove routing, create storage snapshot, and mark for deletion after 7d retention.

Automated enforcement and governance actions
-------------------------------------------
Enforcement is graduated to reduce blast radius:
- Stage 0: Automated notice and dashboard flag.
- Stage 1: Automated rate-limiter profile applied (soft isolation).
- Stage 2: Eviction-friendly routing (move to low-priority pool) + disable cache prefetch hints.
- Stage 3: Snapshot + pause/retire (operator approval required for final deletion).

Automation primitives (operator-facing APIs):
- /api/platform/leases/register (POST) -> registers middleware contract
- /api/platform/leases/renew (POST) -> renew lease programmatically
- CLI: platform-ctl lease register|renew|status
- webhook: lease-expiry-notify -> integrates with PagerDuty/email/Slack

Runbook: on-call operator play (short version)
---------------------------------------------
Trigger: lease-expiry escalations or middleware contract validation failure.
1) Triage: read contract from registry and confirm contact + owner.
2) Check telemetry: is SLI reporting present? Confirm last heartbeat < 5m for health.
3) If telemetry missing but service responsive: send immediate owner ping, apply Stage 1 enforcement profile, mark ticket for 72h review.
4) If service non-responsive or causing platform-level risk: escalate to Stage 2 (eviction pool) and coordinate snapshot.
5) If owner unresponsive after soft windows: follow safe-decommission steps (see Appendix).

Operator checklist (detailed)
---------------------------
- [ ] Retrieve middleware contract: platform-ctl lease status <service>
- [ ] Validate telemetry endpoints (curl <service>:<port>/_status)
- [ ] Review recent SLI dashboards (last 7d) and anomaly markers
- [ ] If stage >=1: apply rate-limit via A/B route modifier and document change
- [ ] If stage >=2: create snapshot, mark caches as invalidated, notify infra-ops

Onboarding checklist for service owners
--------------------------------------
1) Fill middleware contract with required fields and attach to the registration PR.
2) Implement /_status health endpoint returning: {"uptime": seconds, "build": sha, "deps_ok": true}.
3) Emit telemetry: availability events, latency histograms, token counters. Open the onboarding dashboard link and verify graph population within 30 minutes.
4) Confirm sidecar compatibility: sidecar_version must match one of platform-supported entries (see Appendix: supported-versions table).
5) Choose eviction_priority (0 highest, 100 lowest) and provide short justification if < 10.
6) Sign lease (default 6 months) and subscribe a rotating steward (oncall or owner email alias).

YAML examples and CLI quick start
--------------------------------
Service registration example (complete YAML):

  service_name: billing-llm-proxy
  owner: team-billing
  contact: billing-oncall@redwood.ai
  sli_set: [availability, p95-gen-latency, token-cost-per-req]
  health_path: /_status
  lease_expires: 2027-05-01
  sidecar_version: v2.2.0
  eviction_priority: 20
  prefetch_hint: moderate

CLI quick flow:
- platform-ctl lease register --file service-contract.yaml
- platform-ctl lease status billing-llm-proxy
- platform-ctl lease renew billing-llm-proxy --months 6

Enforcement safety and operator controls
---------------------------------------
- All enforcement actions are logged to an immutable audit index and visible to owners.
- Any Stage 3 decommission requires two operator approvals and an owner confirmation can veto within 24h.
- Snapshot artifacts are stored for 30d by default.
- Automated actions are reversible until final deletion window closes.

Metrics, dashboards and alerts (recommended templates)
---------------------------------------------------
Dashboards:
- Service Health Overview: availability (7d), p95, p99, error budget burn rate, lease expiry countdown.
- Platform Lease Inventory: count by expiry bucket, overdue by owner, eviction-priority distribution.
- Contract Compliance: percentage of services meeting minimum telemetry for SLIs.

Alerting examples (PagerDuty rules):
- Critical: SLI availability < 99.5% (page oncall).
- High: Contract missing required telemetry for > 2 hours (page SRE lead, notify owner).
- Medium: Lease expires in 3 days without renewal (email owner + Slack channel).

Rollout plan & milestones
-------------------------
Phase 0 (Pilot, Q1 2027): enroll 30 internal services, refine contract schema, manual renewals.
Phase 1 (Q2 2027): add automation for 30/60/90 day notices and Stage 1 enforcement.
Phase 2 (Q3 2027): enable CLI registration for self-serve onboarding and Stage 2 automated routing changes.
Phase 3 (Q4 2027): full platform-wide enforcement with safety windows and operator dashboards.

Retrospective & feedback loop
----------------------------
We will run a pilot retrospective after Phase 0 covering: false positives, owner friction, and automation flakiness. The retrospective will feed into both platform roadmap and onboarding docs. Owners are expected to provide one example where a lease prevented operational surprise.

Appendix: supported sidecar versions and compatibility table
---------------------------------------------------------
| sidecar_version | supported_since | compatibility_notes |
| v2.0.0 | 2026-01-12 | baseline features (health, metrics) |
| v2.1.0 | 2026-07-05 | adds token counters + prefetch hints |
| v2.2.0 | 2027-01-10 | adds lease-aware cache invalidation |

Appendix: safe-decommission quick steps
------------------------------------
1) Pause new traffic and route 95% away (graceful drain).
2) Snapshot stateful artifacts and persist metadata to object store.
3) Mark caches as invalidated and record snapshot artifact IDs.
4) Notify owner + schedule final deletion (7d).
5) If rollback requested, restore routing and rehydrate caches from snapshots.

Notes and references
--------------------

- See also: platform-operator-runbook and telemetry-contract-evolution page for historical rationale.
- This playbook will be iterated on during pilot run and updated as enforcement automations mature.

End of document
